question: Resolve the DAFRC imputed sponsor-years left unresolved (FY2024: 57 asset and 182 account rows; FY2020-23: 23-46 asset rows a year) by the 990 check: Part IV line 6 'Yes' with a blank Schedule D Part I, count-without-value entries (e.g. Universite de Montreal 714 DAFs / $0) and negative values (USC FY2024 -$53.0m), using PDF images or sponsor audited statements
rationale: Corrected FY2024 total still carries $1.10bn of imputed assets and 10,649 imputed accounts that no filed value can replace automatically

question: Decide whether SDG Impact Fund (EIN 46-2368538; Schedule D Part I $10.10bn FY2021 and FY2022, absent from DAFRC) belongs in the DAF market total, and re-state FY2021-22 market size, growth and concentration with and without it
conclusion_affected: FY2021-22 market size (+4.3-4.5% of DAFRC assets); CR/HHI; FY2022-23 growth
rationale: Outside DAFRC, 413-538 filers a year report DAF value but hold only $0.15-0.89bn; SDG Impact Fund alone is $10.1bn, i.e. 95%+ of the non-DAFRC total in FY2021-22

question: Find DAF sponsors that answer Form 990 Part IV line 6 'No' (or file 990-EZ) yet hold donor-advised funds, by screening Schedule D Part I values and Part III/Schedule O text of all 990 filers with NTEE T30/T31 (community foundations, federated giving) not in DAFRC
rationale: The SOI-extract scan only sees filers that tick Part IV line 6 'Yes'; false negatives are invisible to it

question: Use the Part IX line 14 (information technology) and line 11 fee totals already captured for 5,272 sponsor returns to estimate DAF technology/administration spend per account and per $ of DAF assets by sponsor type and size band
conclusion_affected: Vendor TAM; cost-to-serve per account; buy-vs-build
rationale: Part VII-B itemises only 5,074 of 53,782 contractor engagements >$100k (9.4%) and 985 of 1,512 sponsors list none, so vendor spend must be sized from Part IX totals instead

question: Verify scope and ownership of Northeast Retirement Services (Woburn, MA) as an outsourced donor/fund accounting provider to DAF sponsors (Advisors Charitable Gift Fund, Foundation for the Carolinas, Winston-Salem Foundation) and whether it is a back-office competitor to Ren/Foundant
rationale: Part VII-B shows 'donor accounting', 'fiduciary services' and 'endowment unitization' payments ($1.17m over FY2022-25, sponsors with $3.33bn FY2024 DAF assets); vendor absent from the graph

question: Quantify DAF-to-DAF transfers (grants from one sponsor to another sponsor's DAFs, e.g. Jasper Ridge to Schwab/Fidelity, TIAA to RCF) in Schedule I across the 1,512 sponsors, and net them out of aggregate contributions and grants
conclusion_affected: Market contributions, grants and payout rate
rationale: R2 removes only the terminated sponsors' imputed balances ($0.26bn FY2021, $1.49bn FY2022); the matching flows still inflate both grants (sender) and contributions (recipient)

question: Re-run scripts/mission_dafrc_corrected_totals.py once the 144 FY2025 returns not yet mirrored are available and DAFRC publishes FY2025, and measure how far DAFRC's imputation (FY2024: -$4.88bn assets, +$1.60bn contributions, -286,571 accounts vs filed) biases the first release
conclusion_affected: Nowcast of FY2025 market size; reliability of first-release DAFRC figures
rationale: Filed values beat the imputed ones in 210 of 637 FY2024 rows and fall short in 427; contributions and grants were imputed too low, assets and accounts too high
